ink.role: type, rules, lit segments, inverted fills

unlit.role: a cell that is off; never text

rules: Red is the only hue and it always means 'off target'.
Red never carries meaning alone; a word or a density change says it too.
Intermediate tone is dot density (.nd-screen), never grey fill and never opacity.

faces.name: Dot matrix
faces.why: Ndot and NType82 are proprietary and cannot ship

faces.name: Space Grotesk
faces.why: Drawn from a monospace skeleton, so its squared letterforms share a family of shapes with the dot panel. Chosen against Ndot, NType82 and Lettera Mono LL on the running screens; those three are unlicensable or unbought.

typographyMeta.rootSize: 106.25% (17px default), a percentage so it multiplies the reader's own base size
typographyMeta.i18n: every visible string comes from next-intl; react/jsx-no-literals noStrings is enforced on src/**/*.tsx

shadows.note: No shadow, blur, gradient, translucency or layered surface anywhere. Separation is rules, inversion, or dot density.

motion.policy: one authored animation in the app

animations.name: nd-seek
animations.trigger: a macro strip whose target is not yet met
animations.reducedMotion: animation removed; all transitions clamped to 1ms

breakpoints.note: The desktop view is the phone view with air around it. No sidebar, no second column, no panel reflow.

components.name: Action
components.description: The only button: an inverted block, and the only filled element on a screen besides lit segments.

components.name: Rule
components.description: A 2px ink line. The world here is ruled sheets, not floating boxes.

components.name: Legend
components.what: The uppercase letter-spaced label over a readout. Pass `as` when the legend is the only thing naming its section, so the section has a heading in the document outline; pass `id` when a table below it is named by it.

components.name: Strip
components.what: The bare row of segments a GlyphBar is built from, always aria-hidden. `quiet` draws the shortfall still instead of seeking: the one authored animation belongs to the day's verdict, so a per-meal strip asks for the same arithmetic with the motion taken out.

components.name: TextLink
components.what: An aside, not an intention: underlined running-text link. Action/ActionButton is the filled block; Ghost is the outlined one; this is neither.

components.name: Ghost
components.what: The secondary action: an ink outline at text-xs, uppercase, smaller than Action in every dimension. For a control a row needs but the screen is not about — add a meal, remove an item. A destructive one is not drawn in red: red means a number is off, and a deletion someone asked for is not a fault.

components.name: SmallButton
components.what: A Ghost shrunk to px-2 py-1 — the control a row carries, as opposed to the one a section carries. Four side by side in a list row still read as smaller than the section's one Action.

components.name: Field
components.what: The world's control: label, input, hint and error as one unit. At rest it is an unlit cell — --nd-unlit border, opaque ground, no fill — and focus lands the hard 2px ink ring globals.css gives every focusable thing. aria-invalid swaps the border to --nd-red and the error sentence says the same thing in words. CONTROL_CLASS and CONTROL_BOX are the same string minus w-full, split because width belongs to the caller and Tailwind resolves conflicting utilities by stylesheet order, not attribute order.

components.name: RuledRow
components.what: How every list in this world is drawn: rows separated by `border-t border-nd-unlit` with `first:border-t-0 first:pt-0`, stacked on a phone and turning at `sm` via `sm:flex-row sm:items-baseline sm:justify-between sm:gap-x-6`, with `min-w-0` on the text column and `sm:shrink-0` on the actions. Written as a breakpoint and never as flex-wrap: under flex-wrap whether a row's buttons sit on the name's baseline depends on that row's own meta-text length, so two neighbouring rows in one list disagree.

components.name: Segment
components.description: The atom of the system. State is a string — off, on, over, short — never a boolean.

components.name: GlyphBar
components.description: Label and mono reading on one baseline, a full-width strip of segments, a status line. The strip is aria-hidden; the status line says the same fact in words.

components.name: MealLamps
components.description: One fixed-width lamp per meal, lit if the meal has food in it. Fixed-width because a stretched strip would read as a proportion.

components.name: DotText
components.description: The dot panel. Dots are aria-hidden and the real string sits in an sr-only span, so the panel renders the text rather than duplicating it.

components.name: TabSlot
components.description: Pictogram over label over a lamp. The active slot inverts and lights its lamp; inactive slots keep the lamp's space so nothing shifts.

components.name: FileField
components.what: The file input, drawn in the page's language. The native control labels itself from the browser's locale, so the input is hidden with `sr-only` — focusable, still bound to its label — and a `<label>` styled as an `Action` opens the dialog, with the chosen filename beside it in mono. It lives outside `kit.tsx` because it holds state and `kit.tsx` has to stay importable from a server component.

components.name: TrendChart
components.what: The one chart in the app, and the only continuous quantity that is not segmented. Bars were rejected — they imply a zero baseline, and two kilos on eighty-five is either seven identical bars or a lie about proportion. A dot-matrix scatter on the type's own 5x7 grid was rejected for the opposite reason: at that pitch the meaningful range quantises to about five rows. What is left is a line whose materials carry the hierarchy — the seven-day average in ink at 2.5px with square caps and mitre joins, the individual mornings as --nd-unlit dots (never ink at low alpha, which is a different colour on each of the two grounds), and the top and bottom of the plot as real --nd-unlit hairlines so the vertical extent means something. The current reading sits above it in the same Legend / DotText / unit stack /hoje gives the energy target, at the same displayFontSize. Axis labels are --nd-dim with data-numeric. It sits under a Rule, not inside a card.

components.name: Modal
components.what: A native <dialog> opened with showModal(): 2px ink border, ground fill, no radius and no shadow. Depth is halftone rather than alpha — .nd-modal::backdrop is full-value ink dots of radius 1.2px on a 3px pitch, about 50% coverage, so the page underneath reads as texture and not as text. A scrim would be ink at 60% alpha, which this palette has no word for.

components.name: ConfirmDialog
components.what: role="alertdialog", with the answer that changes nothing written first so showModal() focuses it. On a destructive question the two buttons swap roles rather than colours: keep becomes the filled ActionButton and delete the Ghost, which puts the recommended answer under the eye and under the keyboard at once. Red is never spent on a button — it means a number is off target, and a deletion someone asked for is not a fault.

narrative.overview: DietKit reports the state of one person's body and one day's plan. An instrument shows quantity as light: lamps that are on or off, digits built from dots, a rule where a card would be. The visual world is Nothing OS, pinned by the user and followed literally — the dot face is really built on a 5x7 cell, and the tab pictograms are drawn on that same grid. Reading order is the loop the product is: target, then how far the plan has got with it, then the body that says whether any of it is working.
keyCharacteristics: Two values and one red; every intermediate tone is dot density.
Quantity is rendered as light, never as a filled progress container.
Zero radius, zero shadow, zero gradient. Rules and inversion do all separation.
State is carried at least twice — by light and by words.
One authored motion in the whole app, stilled under prefers-reduced-motion.
One column at every width; the desktop view is the phone view with air around it.
rules: Red means something is off target, and never carries that alone.
--nd-dim is the entire secondary-ink budget; below it, remove the text.
A shaded surface is .nd-screen dots, never a grey fill and never opacity.
Pass .nd-seg a state name, never a boolean — a boolean renders unlit.
Every visible string lives in messages/pt-BR.json.
dos: Carry state by light and by words.
Reach for a rule before a container.
Give a quantity a readout: lamps if countable, a dot panel if it is the answer.
Size a dot panel from one fontSize; everything inside is in em.
donts: No faded type as a hierarchy device.
No radius, shadow or gradient, including the subtle kind.
No rendering the same number in two different voices.
No stretching a small-count indicator to full width.
narrative.notCanonized: The uppercase letter-spaced labels above headings read as eyebrows, which the craft floor bans. They are kept as a carried exception because a legend over a readout is native to the pinned instrument world — not promoted to house style, and still wrong in any other visual world in this codebase. Separately, /dieta, /peso, /alimentos, /perfil and /energia still carry the previous amber/emerald convention and are not described by this document.
